geographical_area: City of Bari (urban Barese). The profile follows the city norm; Murgia, the province and the Salento (a different southern Apulian group, not covered and never mixed in) differ.
linguistic_classification: Apulian (Neapolitan-type upper-southern Italo-Romance group), Barese variety; traditionally called a dialect.
orthographic_conventions: No official Barese orthography exists. The profile uses an accented popular spelling: unstressed final vowels written with their etymological letter although pronounced as schwa; accents mark vowel quality and tell homographs apart (ué/uè, nù/nu, pésce/pèsce); apostrophe for aphaeresis and elision ('ngàse, 'mmàghene); consonant doubling after function words (che ttè, pe nnù); phonetic schwa spellings of Wiktionary converted to this convention.
description_en: Urban Barese of Bari: schwa-reduced vowels, metaphony marking gender and number (bbuéne/bbóne, jìdde/jédde), articles u/la/le, tené for possession, avé a + infinitive for obligation, enclitic kinship possessives (màmete, fràtete), stà a + verb progressives and ca as complementizer. Voice: teasing banter, mock praise and hyperbole around the local insult tremóne.
description_it: Il barese urbano di Bari: vocali ridotte a schwa, metafonia che distingue genere e numero (bbuéne/bbóne, jìdde/jédde), articoli u/la/le, tené per il possesso, avé a + infinito per il dovere, possessivi enclitici con i nomi di parentela (màmete, fràtete), perifrasi progressiva con stà e ca come complementatore. Tono: sfottò, lode ironica e iperbole attorno all'insulto locale tremóne.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Barese insult: idiot, dumbass, wanker; literally 'wank'. Between friends it is banter, to strangers a real insult.
identifier_word.meaning_it: Insulto barese: coglione, idiota, imbranato; letteralmente 'masturbazione'.
identifier_word.attestation: Wiktionary has the entry trimone (chiefly Bari) with the senses 'wank' and 'idiot' and local pronunciations (Bari, Molfetta); Patrimoni Linguistici and Barinedita discuss meaning and usage and give etymological hypotheses, which this profile does not assert; en.wikipedia (Barese dialect) quotes the exclamation 'Ce ttremóne!'. The spelling 'trimone' is the Italianised, commercial form used as the mode id; the dialect text writes tremóne.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review yet: all example sentences are AI-illustrative, built on documented rules and attested items.
Barese has no official orthography; spellings in the sources vary (iì/ji, ié/jè, schwa written or omitted) and this profile picks one form and lists variants.

Most sources are Wikipedia, Wiktionary and local popular web (reliability medium); only Andriani (2017) is a high-reliability academic source, so the grammar core rests on it and on the Italian Wikipedia grammar.

The avé paradigm of en.wikipedia (agghiá/adda/java/amma/avita/avonne) conflicts with other sources and was not adopted; the profile uses the forms of the lexicon (àgghie, è, à, àmme, avìte, ànne/ònne).
Only forms attested in the lexicon or documented in the sources are used; paradigm cells without a documented form are avoided rather than guessed, so some tenses are under-described.
The etymology of trimone is unsettled; the profile makes no etymological claim.
Copyrighted dictionaries and grammars of Barese were not consulted.
